package_info.why_malicious: The report does not describe any specific malicious package or code. Instead, it discusses general risks, vulnerabilities, and best practices for securing the software supply chain, without analyzing a particular malicious package.

behavioral_signatures: Introduction of unauthorized or unreviewed open-source packages into the codebase
Unexpected or unexplained changes to software configurations or build scripts
Use of third-party code that has not been vetted or scanned for vulnerabilities
file_indicators: Presence of open-source package files that have not undergone review or curation
Binary files originating from unknown or untrusted sources within the project repository
network_indicators: Outbound network connections initiated during build or deployment processes that are not part of the expected workflow
Connections from CI/CD pipelines to domains or IP addresses known to be malicious or untrusted
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement continuous monitoring and curation of all open-source packages at the point of entry. Scan both source and binary code for vulnerabilities using automated tools. Analyze proprietary code for security issues and monitor for abnormal network activity during all phases of the software development lifecycle. Employ contextual analysis to reduce false positives and ensure ongoing collaboration between development and security teams to promptly identify and respond to supply chain threats.
